description: Measuring attention to a masked stimulus over 590 ms after onset, Webb and colleagues found larger fluctuations when people were unaware of the stimulus than when aware, with similar overall magnitude, read as awareness stabilizing attention (Webb et al. 2016b, as reported by Graziano).
limitations: Reported secondhand in Graziano 2018. The original paper is not downloaded here.

sources.quote: The fluctuations were significantly greater when the participants were unaware of the stimulus than when they were aware of it.
